normative_statement: Each compilation SHALL establish an identifiable authorized governance-source baseline.
Each material source SHALL have a stable source identifier.
Each material source SHALL record version or revision status where applicable.
Each material source SHALL identify its issuing authority or authority basis.
Each material source SHALL record declared applicability to the compilation scope.
Each material source SHALL record effective, superseded, withdrawn, or equivalent lifecycle status.
Each material source SHALL preserve provenance sufficient to identify origin and acquisition path.
Explicitly excluded material sources SHALL be recorded when their exclusion affects scope or completeness claims.
Disputed or unknown source applicability SHALL be represented as uncertainty, limitation, escalation, or refusal rather than silently resolved by the compiler.
Source authorization for compilation SHALL NOT be represented as proof of legal validity, normative legitimacy, constitutionality, substantive correctness, or proportionality.
Each compilation SHALL declare the scope to which its normative and completeness claims apply.
The declared scope SHALL identify the governed domain and target classes.
The declared scope SHALL identify applicable organizations, tenants, or jurisdictional boundaries where material.
The declared scope SHALL identify actors and authority relationships material to the governed actions.
The declared scope SHALL identify effective period or temporal assumptions where material.
The declared scope SHALL identify applicable constitutional and system invariants.
The declared scope SHALL identify material threat/failure assumptions and exclusions.
An implementation SHALL NOT make an unqualified completeness claim when the relevant scope boundary is undeclared.
Material interpretation decisions SHALL be attributable to an identified authority or authorized process.
An interpretation record SHALL identify the affected source or requirement.
An interpretation record SHALL record the selected interpretation and material scope.
An interpretation record SHOULD record alternatives considered when they materially affect authority or behavior.
An interpretation record SHALL record material assumptions and unresolved uncertainty.
AI- or tool-generated interpretation SHALL NOT become institutionally authoritative solely because it was generated automatically.
Irreducible ambiguity SHALL NOT be silently converted into deterministic semantics.
When ambiguity remains material, the implementation SHALL use authorized interpretation, bounded discretion, narrowed scope, indeterminate/escalation semantics, or refusal.
Interpretation changes SHALL be evaluated for downstream model/package impact.
Governance requirements SHALL remain traceable to authorized source and interpretation provenance.
Traceability SHALL permit navigation from source to canonical model elements.
Traceability SHALL permit navigation from canonical model elements to source/interpretation basis.
Target artifacts SHALL remain traceable to the canonical model elements from which they were projected.
Validation evidence SHALL identify the model/package/object to which it applies.
Approval and issuance records SHALL bind to the exact model or package identity approved.
Activation records SHALL bind to the exact package identity and runtime scope activated.
Runtime evidence SHOULD identify the active package/governance version used for the decision.
A GIR document SHALL have stable identity and version.
A GIR document SHALL identify the Governance Compilation specification version to which it claims conformance.
A GIR document SHALL identify its declared scope.
GIR cross-object references SHALL use stable identifiers rather than display names alone.
The GIR SHALL represent governance requirements and their source/interpretation linkage.
The GIR SHALL represent governed actions and typed targets/parameters sufficient for the declared authority boundary.
The GIR SHALL represent the Permitted Action Set separately from current authorization conditions.
The GIR SHALL represent applicable authority and authority provenance.
The GIR SHALL represent mandatory evidence semantics and trust conditions required by the profile.
The GIR SHALL represent applicable constitutional and system invariants.
The GIR SHALL represent explicit refusal, indeterminate, or escalation behavior where applicable.
The GIR SHALL represent temporal/lifecycle conditions that affect applicability or authority.
The GIR SHALL represent assumptions, limitations, profiles, and mandatory extensions.
An unknown mandatory GIR extension affecting authority, evidence, target-state, composition, or closure SHALL NOT be silently ignored.
An interchange implementation claiming GIR conformance SHALL preserve all mandatory core semantics through serialization/deserialization.
Computational capability SHALL NOT be treated as evidence that an action is inside the Permitted Action Set.
An action outside the active Permitted Action Set SHALL NOT become authorized solely because it can be proposed or executed.
Membership in the Permitted Action Set SHALL NOT by itself authorize a concrete action.
Current authorization SHALL be evaluated against applicable actor/principal authority, scope, target, state, time, evidence, and invariants as required by the profile.
Authority assertions SHALL be bound to authority provenance.
Authority provenance SHALL identify the role, office, delegation, or institutional basis from which the asserted authority derives.
Authority provenance SHALL identify scope and validity limits where applicable.
Authority provenance SHALL represent revocation or supersession status where applicable.
A revoked or expired authority SHALL NOT satisfy a current authorization condition.
An authorization decision SHALL NOT silently broaden the Permitted Action Set.
Each Governance-Defined Action Region SHALL have stable identity and version.
Each region SHALL define membership or predicate semantics sufficient for deterministic applicability within the declared profile.
Region provenance SHALL identify the source/requirement basis for its governance treatment.
Region overlap MAY occur but SHALL be resolved through explicit applicability/composition semantics.
Region specificity SHALL NOT by itself authorize weakening a broader mandatory obligation.
Every covered action/context requiring transition governance SHALL resolve to treatment or an explicit unknown/indeterminate/refusal status.
Region-to-contract mapping gaps within a declared covered region SHALL be detected or explicitly classified.
Region changes SHALL trigger impact analysis of affected mappings/contracts/packages.
Each Complete Transition Contract SHALL contain pre-state semantics.
Each Complete Transition Contract SHALL contain current authorization semantics.
Each Complete Transition Contract SHALL contain required pre-commit evidence semantics.
Each Complete Transition Contract SHALL contain target-state semantics.
Each Complete Transition Contract SHALL contain required post-commit evidence semantics.
Each Complete Transition Contract SHALL contain outcome-specific closure semantics.
CTC references to authority, evidence, invariants, target states, or external dependencies SHALL be resolvable within the applicable package/profile boundary.
CTC structural well-formedness SHALL NOT be represented as proof of satisfiability.
CTC satisfiability SHALL NOT be represented as proof of target-state or closure reachability.
Mandatory pre-commit evidence SHALL remain mandatory through composition absent an explicitly authorized substitution/override.
CTC changes SHALL preserve source and version provenance.
Human judgment points within a CTC SHALL identify the authority responsible for that judgment or escalation.
Composition SHALL be defined per CTC component rather than by one undifferentiated combining rule.
Each profile using composition SHALL define permitted composition operators and conflict behavior.
Composition SHALL NOT silently discard a mandatory obligation.
Any weakening, substitution, exception, waiver, or override of a mandatory obligation SHALL be explicitly modeled and authorized.
An authorized non-monotonic rule SHALL identify affected obligation, scope, conditions, provenance, and authorizing authority.
File order, rule order, last-write-wins behavior, or specificity alone SHALL NOT constitute authority to weaken governance.
Composition conflicts that cannot be resolved under declared rules SHALL produce an explicit indeterminate/refusal/escalation result.
Composition results SHOULD be reproducible under a declared canonicalization/equivalence criterion.
Required evidence SHALL be typed or otherwise semantically identifiable.
Required evidence SHALL identify subject or target binding where material.
Required evidence SHALL identify freshness/validity conditions where material.
Required evidence SHALL identify admissible producing source/interface where the profile depends on source qualification.
Replay-sensitive evidence SHALL define anti-replay requirements.
An authenticated evidence object SHALL NOT be treated as necessarily true evidence content.
Evidence profiles SHOULD identify independence or corroboration requirements where material.
Evidence profiles SHOULD identify compromise/revocation assumptions for evidence sources.
Missing mandatory evidence SHALL NOT silently satisfy an authorization, target-state, or closure condition.
Evidence used for closure SHALL remain linked to the outcome/target to which it applies.
A target projection SHALL preserve authority boundaries from the approved canonical model.
A target projection SHALL NOT grant authority outside the canonical Permitted Action Set.
A target projection SHALL preserve mandatory authorization conditions applicable to projected actions.
A target projection SHALL preserve mandatory invariant obligations.
A target projection SHALL preserve mandatory evidence obligations.
A target projection SHALL NOT claim closure under conditions weaker than the canonical closure semantics.
Projection limitations or unsupported semantics SHALL be declared rather than silently omitted.
A consumer that cannot represent a mandatory semantic feature SHALL refuse compatibility or require an explicitly approved profile transformation.
Each compiled governance package SHALL have stable immutable identity and version.
Each package SHALL include integrity metadata sufficient to bind lifecycle records to exact content.
Each package manifest SHALL identify the canonical model identity/version/digest.
Each package manifest SHALL identify the source-baseline identity.
Each package manifest SHALL identify compiler/version/configuration identity sufficient for the profile.
Each package manifest SHALL identify the target/runtime profile.
Each package manifest SHALL include an artifact inventory with integrity identifiers.
Each package manifest SHALL identify declared scope and invariant profile.
Each package manifest SHALL identify known exclusions, limitations, and unresolved build-time assumptions.
Mutable validation/approval/activation status SHOULD be represented in detached records bound to the immutable package identity.
Package validation SHALL be performed separately from canonical-model verification.
A package SHALL NOT be considered authoritatively issued solely because it is structurally valid or executable.
Authoritative issuance SHALL be attributable to an authorized actor or process.
Activation SHALL be represented as a lifecycle transition distinct from issuance.
Activation SHALL verify exact package identity and integrity.
Activation SHALL verify applicable issuance/approval status.
Activation SHALL verify non-revoked/non-suspended lifecycle status.
Activation SHALL verify compatibility with required runtime/profile semantics.
Activation SHALL bind the package to a defined runtime scope.
Activation SHALL enforce effective/expiration timing when applicable.
Failure of a mandatory activation precondition SHALL cause structural refusal or a defined non-active status.
Supersession, suspension, revocation, and rollback SHALL be distinguishable lifecycle states/actions.
A runtime consumer SHALL identify the active package/version used for a governance decision.
A runtime consumer SHALL verify compatibility with mandatory semantics and extensions.
A runtime consumer SHALL obtain required current authority, evidence, and state.
A runtime consumer SHALL preserve scope, tenant, and jurisdiction boundaries represented by the active package/profile.
A runtime consumer SHALL apply defined missing-information and indeterminate-result behavior.
A runtime consumer SHALL bind a decision to the exact proposal/action and target evaluated.
A runtime consumer SHALL preserve refusal, escalation, and hold semantics.
Where eligibility can become stale before commitment, the runtime profile SHALL require commitment-boundary revalidation or equivalent atomic/fenced protection.
Runtime authorization at evaluation time SHALL NOT be presumed valid at commitment when a relevant condition has changed.
Runtime evidence SHOULD bind decision time and commitment time where distinct.
A runtime allow/permit decision SHALL NOT be treated as proof that the target state was achieved.
A runtime receipt SHALL NOT by itself establish deployment non-bypassability.
Target-state verification SHALL evaluate the applicable target-state semantics using qualified observation/evidence.
Successful request dispatch or API response SHALL NOT automatically satisfy target-state semantics unless the governance explicitly defines it as sufficient.
Closure SHALL be outcome-specific where terminal outcomes have different obligations.
Successful closure SHALL require satisfaction of applicable authorization and closure conditions.
Successful execution SHALL NOT be treated as governance closure without required closure evidence.
Closure safety SHALL be paired with reachability/nonvacuity analysis when the profile makes a meaningful success claim.
Probabilistic evidence SHALL be governed by explicit deterministic decision/escalation semantics.
Closure evidence SHALL remain reconstructibly linked to the governed transition and outcome.
A security claim SHALL state material trust assumptions within its declared scope.
Cryptographic authenticity SHALL NOT be generalized to truth, correctness, independence, freshness, or target binding without separate evidence.
A profile relying on signed artifacts SHALL identify signing authority, key custody, trust anchors, verification policy, rotation/expiry, compromise response, and revocation.
A package requirement for non-bypassable enforcement SHALL NOT be represented as deployment evidence of non-bypassability.
A deployment non-bypassability claim SHALL identify the consequence-producing boundary assessed.
A deployment non-bypassability claim SHALL include evidence addressing alternate privileged, administrative, maintenance, or direct target paths where material.
A deployment non-bypassability claim SHALL identify configuration/topology/identity/dependency changes that invalidate the claim.
Missing, stale, revoked, unverifiable, or incompatible mandatory security evidence SHALL NOT silently default to authorization.
A conformance claim SHALL identify the specification and exact version.
A conformance claim SHALL identify the conformance object.
A conformance claim SHALL identify applicable profiles.
A conformance claim SHALL identify the bounded scope/domain/jurisdiction covered.
A conformance claim SHALL identify the evidence/assurance basis.
A conformance claim SHALL identify exclusions and known limitations.
A conformance claim SHALL identify effective period or validity conditions where applicable.
A conformance claim SHALL identify unresolved findings or compensating controls where material.
Partial conformance SHALL NOT be presented as full-lifecycle conformance.
Conditional conformance SHALL identify the external condition/dependency and invalidation trigger.
Conformance of one object SHALL NOT be represented as conformance of unrelated lifecycle objects.
Conformance SHALL NOT be represented as a general legal opinion or guarantee of lawful, ethical, safe, or correct outcomes.
Each profile SHALL have stable identity, version, and status.
Each profile SHALL identify supported specification version(s).
Each profile SHALL declare applicability/scope and required core capabilities.
Each profile SHALL identify added normative requirements and mandatory extensions.
A profile SHALL NOT silently redefine a core term.
A profile SHALL NOT weaken a core mandatory requirement unless the core explicitly defines that requirement as profile-variable.
An unknown mandatory extension that can affect authority, evidence, composition, target state, or closure SHALL cause incompatibility/refusal rather than silent ignore.
A rights-affecting profile SHOULD define contestability/redress semantics where required by the governing institution or law.
A distributed-transition profile SHALL identify atomicity, compensation, partial-commit, recovery-authority, and composite-closure semantics that it claims to support.
The v0.1 distributed-transition profile SHALL be represented as experimental rather than as a solved core property.
A compiler-qualification claim SHALL identify the actual human/software/AI-assisted/organizational capability being relied upon.
A qualification claim SHALL identify the intended-use scope for which the capability is qualified.
A qualification claim SHALL identify supported specification/profile versions and target projection classes.

Qualification evidence SHOULD address semantic fidelity, traceability, diagnostics, provenance, reproducibility/equivalence, configuration control, security, and negative testing proportionate to intended use.
Compiler qualification SHALL NOT be represented as package-specific validation.
Package validation SHALL NOT be represented as proof that the compiler capability is generally qualified.
AI-assisted compilation SHALL identify the role delegated to the probabilistic component and the control by which its output becomes authoritative.
AI-generated interpretation SHALL NOT become authoritative solely because it was generated by an AI system.
Where byte-identical reproducibility is not required or possible, the qualification profile SHALL define the equivalence criterion actually claimed.
A qualification evidence package SHOULD identify dependencies and configuration baseline material to the claim.
Material changes to compiler semantics, AI model/provider/configuration, dependencies, adapters, or build/security environment SHALL be assessed for requalification impact.
A material change SHALL invalidate affected qualification claims until re-established.
An assurance record SHALL identify the claim supported by each material evidence item.
Evidence for one claim SHALL NOT silently substitute for evidence of a different claim.
Authenticated evidence SHALL NOT be treated as necessarily truthful/correct evidence content.
A profile depending on evidence accuracy SHALL identify the observation/source-qualification/corroboration assumptions supporting that claim.
Assurance results SHOULD identify their evidence level or method.
A bounded executable check SHALL NOT be described as machine-checked universal proof.
An implementation-conformance result SHALL NOT be described as empirical effectiveness without operational evidence.
Property results SHOULD distinguish satisfied, unsatisfied, indeterminate, not applicable, and not evaluated statuses where relevant.
A solver/tool result SHALL NOT automatically determine institutional package disposition unless the profile assigns that authority.
Higher-consequence assurance cases SHOULD link claims, arguments, evidence, assumptions/context, and limitations.
Continuing-assurance profiles SHOULD identify source/authority/evidence/deployment changes that invalidate prior claims.
An independence claim SHOULD identify material organizational, financial, technical, and evidence-access relationships.
An operating-protocol conformance claim SHALL identify which semantic operations it supports.
Logical producer, repository, validator, issuance, activation, runtime-consumer, and evidence/status responsibilities SHALL remain distinguishable even when implemented by combined components.
Before active consumption, exact package identity/integrity SHALL be verified.
Before active consumption, supported specification/profile semantics SHALL be verified.
Before active consumption, authoritative issuance status SHALL be verified.
Before active consumption, revoked/suspended status SHALL be evaluated.
Before active consumption, scope/target applicability SHALL be evaluated.
Before active consumption, effective/expiration timing SHALL be evaluated where applicable.
Unknown mandatory extensions SHALL cause incompatibility/refusal rather than permissive fallback.
Integrity mismatch, missing issuance, lifecycle invalidity, scope mismatch, or equivalent mandatory failure SHALL NOT silently select a permissive fallback.
A consumer caching lifecycle or authority state SHALL define freshness/consistency behavior appropriate to the profile.
A stale cache SHALL NOT authorize commitment after a material revocation/change when the profile requires current state.
An interoperability result SHOULD identify producer/consumer versions, profile versions, package identity, operations/vectors exercised, results, deviations, and limitations.
